vectors.name: formats-yaml/temporals/native-date-resolves-with-no-schema
vectors.comment: YAML's core schema resolves a bare ISO-8601-looking scalar to date with no schema involved -- unlike JSON, which would leave this as a string until stage 2.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/sharp-edges/bare-time-resolves-to-sexagesimal-integer-not-a-time
vectors.comment: YAML's core schema has no standalone time type. A bare 12:00:00 resolves to the integer 43200 (twelve hours in seconds) -- YAML's own behavior, not an Omnist choice, and there is no read-side workaround once the parser has already produced an integer. Confirmed live against the reference implementation.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/sharp-edges/norway-problem-bare-on-key-resolves-to-boolean-and-is-rejected
vectors.comment: YAML 1.1's core schema resolves on/off/yes/no/true/false (in various cases) as booleans, not strings -- a bare `on:` key parses to the boolean true. Since a label MUST be a string, a reader MUST refuse to build a Document from a boolean-keyed mapping rather than silently coercing it. This is the exact failure mode that breaks an unquoted GitHub Actions `on:` trigger block. Confirmed live: the reference implementation reports this as a shape/label error, not a YAML-specific one -- quoting the key ("on":) is the only workaround, and there is none on the read side once resolution has already happened.

vectors.name: formats-yaml/encoding/doubled-leading-bom-is-rejected
vectors.comment: D-21: D-15 consumes exactly one leading U+FEFF and stops. The text that remains is parsed by this surface's own grammar, which admits no U+FEFF as content at offset zero, so the second mark is a syntax error. The position is 1:1 because it is computed on the text remaining after the strip. One of the two surfaces where this vector is red today. YAML 1.2 permits a leading BOM in its own right and the common libraries strip one before the grammar sees it -- layered under D-15's strip that is a second, undeclared strip, and two byte-different inputs build one Document with no diagnostic saying which byte was discarded. That is the outcome D-15 exists to prevent, so D-21 requires the reader to pre-check and reject. Measured: the reference accepts this input and returns the same Document as the single-BOM form (DIV-4).
